uncited: **Inputs:** A trained set of 3D Gaussians (positions, covariances, opacities, spherical harmonics coefficients) and a set of training views (camera poses and intrinsics).
**Outputs:** A static global ordering of splats based on contribution, and a dynamic rendering pipeline that selects splats based on this order and viewport context.
**Training Views:** A list of camera parameters and image dimensions.
**Contribution Map:** A global aggregation structure storing the count of times each Gaussian index appears in the top-$k$ contributors for any pixel in any training view.
**Splat Order:** A sorted list of Gaussian indices, sorted descending by their total contribution count.
**Render Training Views:** For each training view, render the scene using all 3D Gaussians.
During rasterization, for each pixel, identify the top-$k$ Gaussians that contribute most to the final color (e.g., highest opacity-weighted depth contribution or alpha coverage).
**Aggregate Contributions:** Initialize a global counter array $C$ of size $N$ (total number of Gaussians) to zero.
For every occurrence of a Gaussian $i$ in the top-$k$ lists from Step 1, increment $C[i]$.
**Create Ordering:** Sort all Gaussian indices $i \in \{0, \dots, N-1\}$ based on the values in $C$ in descending order.
**Dynamic Selection:** To render or stream a scene, select the first $M = \lfloor p \times N \rfloor$ splats from $O$.
**Viewport Integration:** Integrate the static ordering $O$ with real-time viewport context.
Changing the training set requires recomputing the order.
*   **Time Complexity:** The pre-processing step (contribution calculation) requires rendering all training views with all Gaussians.

If $V$ is the number of training views, $N$ the number of Gaussians, and $P$ the number of pixels per view, the complexity is roughly $O(V \cdot N \cdot P)$ for rendering and $O(N \log N)$ for sorting.
The rendering step itself is $O(M \cdot P)$ where $M$ is the number of splats rendered.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Requires storing the contribution counts ($O(N)$) and the ordered indices ($O(N)$).
The rendering memory is proportional to the number of splats currently being rendered.
The initial quality is an approximation; fine details may be missing until more splats are loaded.
*   **When not to use:** When full fidelity is required immediately without progressive refinement.
